cases.rejectionReceipt: The present dating interval touches the event boundary; the pilot has not established a securely pre-event textual form independent of the predicted fall.
Babylonian domination, Jerusalem's destruction, exile and return supply different admissible endpoints; the textual forms and seventy-year semantics require a source-layer audit before scoring.

This is admitted as an adverse interpretation-and-repair case, not yet as predictive calibration; source layers and the relation between Nebuchadnezzar and later Alexander receptions must remain separate.
The source-date inference is entangled with the apparent transition from accurate sequence to inaccurate endpoint; it is a control for ex-eventu identification, not an independent prediction witness.
Excellent internal test form, but the same narrative reports oracle and outcome; it can train annotation, not establish foresight.
A source-date interval spanning AD 70 cannot independently validate pre-event prediction without an earlier securely dated textual witness or source layer.
External famine evidence can support historical retrodiction, but the surviving prophecy report postdates the event and cannot validate foresight.
Open forecasts cannot calibrate a rule; the unbounded 'may end later' clause also prevents 2060 from acting as a terminal falsification date.

decision: No predictive ranking is identified. Expand and provenance-close the calibration registry before fitting hermeneutic operators.
claimBoundary: This audit measures source admission only; it neither validates nor falsifies divine prophecy.
